about.what: Hand-adjudicated categories for real cinema listings. Each row carries the input a categoriser sees - title, runtime and the listing description - alongside the category a human judged correct. Built while evaluating TypeSafe Jev against the incumbent LLM in September 2026, but it is not specific to either: it scores anything that maps a listing to one of the categories in CLAUDE.md.
about.selfContained: Rows embed their own input text on purpose. The listings themselves fall out of retrieved-data and transformed-data within weeks, and showingId is kept only for provenance - nothing here needs those releases to still exist.
about.notABenchmark: Do NOT read an accuracy figure off the whole file. The rows were drawn three different ways and none of the three is a random sample of listings. Score a sample, then weight by the band populations recorded below - see howToScore.
about.scoring: A label of "either" means the listing is genuinely ambiguous; exclude those rows from scoring. A label containing "|" lists acceptable alternatives ("tv|movie"), and an answer matching ANY of them counts as correct.
about.howToScore: For a population estimate, score the blind-sample rows within each confidence band, then weight each band by bandPopulations - the band sizes measured across the 243 comparable listings in the 14 venues below. The disagreement rows are deliberately biased and must be left out of any such estimate.

samples.disagreement: Rows where the incumbent LLM and Jev gave different answers. Selected BY model behaviour, so biased - useful for finding failure modes, useless for measuring accuracy.
samples.gate-sample: Blind random sample of rows below the 0.85 confidence gate, stratified ~10 per band. Labelled without sight of either model answer.
samples.high-sample: Blind random sample of rows at or above 0.85 confidence. Labelled without sight of either model answer.
samples.held-out-1: Simple random sample from 8 venues not used to tune anything at the time. Spent afterwards: the 0.60 gate and the institut-francais fix were both derived from its errors, so it no longer measures generalisation.
samples.held-out-2: Every comparable row from 14 venues never used in any earlier sample or fix. The cleanest generalisation evidence in the file.

rows.title: Passing through Paris
rows.description:
Passing through Paris

France becomes the focus of this programme, with two shorts exploring Paris’s architecture, while the last film looks at race and immigration through a satirical and comedic lens.

Le cimetière du Père Lachaise

Père Lachaise Cemetery

France 1978. Director Sarah Maldoror. 7min. Video. With English subtitles

L’ architecture d’inspiration étrangère à Paris

France 1979. Director Sarah Maldoror. 3min. Video. With English subtitles

UK Premiere of 4K restoration: Un dessert pour Constance

A Dessert for Constance

France 1979. Director Sarah Maldoror. 59min. Digital 4K (restoration). With English subtitles

Restored in 4K with the support of Centre national du cinéma et de l'image animée.

Total film programme running time 69min

A camera roams the famous flagstones and foliage of Père Lachaise cemetery, to the sound of poems such as Liberté by Paul Éluard. Paris is regarded through the prism of its architecture that has drawn on foreign inspiration. And in Un dessert pour Constance, which acknowledges the culinary prowess of French cuisine, comedy combats racist stereotypes and nationalist ideas via a portrait of the daily lives of African migrants in Paris, who mobilise to allow one of their own to return home to die.

The screening of Passing through Paris on Monday 7 September will include a discussion curated and hosted by programmer Abiba Coulibaly.

rows.description:
All Is Politics

+ intro by Carine Harmand, Curator at Tate Liverpool

Sarah Maldoror points her camera at a number of influential African and diasporic figures through her beautifully filmed and intimate portraits.

Alberto Carlisky

France 1980. Director Sarah Maldoror. 4min. Digital. With English subtitles

Portrait d’une femme africaine

France 1985. Director Sarah Maldoror. 3min. Digital. With English subtitles

Christiane Diop

France 1985. Director Sarah Maldoror. 5min. Digital. With English subtitles

Un sénégalais en Normandie

France 1986. Director Sarah Maldoror. 13min. Digital. With English subtitles

UK Premiere of restoration: Aimé Césaire – un homme une terre

Aimé Césaire, A Man, A Land

France 1977. Director Sarah Maldoror. 57min. Digital (restoration). With English subtitles

Total film programme running time 82min

A portrait of Argentinian sculptor Alberto Carlisky, who replaces his militant and journalistic life in Buenos Aires with his role as an assistant to Paris-based Cubist sculptor Ossip Zadkine, eventually becoming an artist himself. A brief but intimate portrait of a young Senegalese cook in a workers hostel finds her keen to travel through France but taking umbrage at the term ‘immigrant’. Christiane Diop, the first Black woman to run a major publishing house in Paris, is the subject of a portrait that also features Sophie Mondesir, a French illustrator of West Indian-Guadeloupean origin. The testimonies of Senegalese poet Léopold Sédar Senghor’s neighbours are intertwined with his poems and conversations about his life and career. And in Un homme, une terre, Sarah Maldoror and Aimé Césaire discuss surrealism, poetry and the future of Martinique, which he likens to a tree.
Contains scenes of cockfighting and racist language.

rows.title: All to Mexico!
rows.description:
All to Mexico!

Here, Sarah Maldoror’s work focuses on two Soviet artists, painter Vlady Kibalchich and writer Victor Serge.

L’hôpital de Leningrad

Leningrad Hospital

France 1982. Director Sarah Maldoror. With Roger Blin, Rüdiger Vogler, Victor Garrivier, Anne Wiazemsky. 52min. Digital. With English subtitles

World Premiere of 4K restoration: Vlady

France-Mexico 1989. Director Sarah Maldoror. 24min. Digital 4K (restoration). With English subtitles

Total film programme running time 76min

In Mexico, Russian refugee and painter Vlady Kibalchich Rusakov completes an eight-year project to paint the frescoes in San Felipe Neri chapel, which the Mexican government has converted into the Miguel Lerdo library. He would have liked to paint landscapes, but cannot detach himself from his history, and reproduces the world revolutions. Leningrad Hospital, highlighting Sarah Maldoror’s denunciation of political imprisonment – a key element of her work – adheres to Russian writer Victor Serge’s text as it denounces the psychiatric hospitals that Stalin’s state police placed the leader’s opponents.

The screening of All to Mexico! on Wednesday 3 September will be introduced by season curator Annouchka de Andrade.

rows.title: Away Up North – An Evening Of Movie Mavericks from Finland
rows.description:
After its milestone 40th anniversary, the legendary Midnight Sun Film Festival makes a one-off pilgrimage to the home of film history, the Cinema Museum in London. Founded in the Finnish Arctic Circle by Director brothers Aki and Mika Kaurismäki, the renowned international film festival has been exciting movie fans at the top of the world for decades.
London will be treated to a showcase of films curated from the vaults of the Finnish Film Archive. In the true spirit of the festival that never sleeps, there will be new discoveries and contemporary classics from Finnish mavericks. The highlight will be live accompaniment by notable Finnish musicians Lau Nau and Henri Utan K. This continues the festival’s long legacy of reinterpreting silent cinema with fresh, contemporary live scores.
The evening closes with a rare 35mm screening of Mika Kaurismäki’s wisecracking cult film The Liar (1981), written and starring his brother Aki. It is preceded by Aki’s tribute to the Lumiére brothers, The Foundry (2007) and festival favourite Finnish Frustrations (1969), a groundbreaking feminist short by Eija Kaarresalo-Kasari.
Tervetuloa – a warm welcome.
7PM: INTRO
Midnight Sun Film Festival (Heikki Ortamo, 1987, 9min)
The greatest film festival (anti-)promotional short ever made, which explains why Midnight Sun is a unique event for both Finnish film buffs and some of the stellar international talents who attend it. The latter also appear in this hilarious guide to a very Finland way of sharing films.
Format: 35mm.
7.15 PM: PART ONE
Jean Sibelius at Home (Aho & Soldan, 1927, 6 min) – live score by Lau Nau
Late autumn, 1927, at the home of maestro Jean Sibelius in Ainola, Finland. A charming, little, free-form documentary about Sibelius and his family celebrating an autumn day. Heidi and Margareta Sibelius play four-hand piano, Aino is busy in the garden, the morning papers and a cigar start the master’s day. A classic from Finnish documentary pioneers Heikki Aho and Björn Soldan.
Format 16mm.
Once Upon Time There Was Winter – and Snow (Unknown,1934, 6 min) – live score by Lau Nau
The Finnish realm of snow and ice. In this unknown gem from almost a century ago, the progress of an icebreaker ship feels like a symbol of the modernisation and urbanisation of the world: slow but inevitable. The relationship with nature is still carefree. Joys of winter are taken for granted, and the urban core of Finland produces images that may seem like a fairytale to an outsider. Greetings from a time of innocence.
Format: DCP.
Varala, Women’s Paradise (Aimo Jäderholm, 1947, 9 min) – live score by Henri Utan K
Summer 1947, a poetic, skillfully rhythmic documentary about Varala, the legendary women’s physical education institute. Located in a scenic peninsula on the shores of Lake Pyhäjärvi, it is the pride of Finland’s second city, Tampere. For decades Varala has been a haven for women’s sports. “Even though we only appear to be playing, we are doing it for the good of the fatherland.”
Format: 16mm.
Rocky VI (Aki Kaurismäki, 1986, 9 min)
A musical parody of Rocky IV (1985) topped with Aki Kaurismäki’s singular deadpan humour. Rocky, played by Silu Seppänen of Leningrad Cowboys fame, defends the Free World and battles the hulking Siberian boxer, Igor. Has Rocky finally met his match?
Format: 35mm.
A Planet Far Away (Juha Kuosmanen, 2023, 16 min) – live score by Lau Nau & Henri Utan K
Using handmade trickery, silent cinema is reawakened with a modern twist. From the Cannes-winning director Juho Kuosmanen (Compartment No. 6), the final instalment of the celebrated silent trilogy tells a story of lighthouse-keeper Marlanda and her little brother Maximilian. It’s a bedtime story about the end of everything and the extraordinary attempts to survive it. But it’s not bedtime, it’s just the interval.
Format: DCP.
8:15 PM: INTERMISSION
8:30 PM: PART TWO
The Foundry (Aki Kaurismäki, 2007, 4 min)
Another proletarian life slice, this time set in Karkkila, hometown of director Aki Kaurismäki. Workers at a foundry eat their lunch while watching the Lumiére brothers’ film La Sortie de l’usine Lumière à Lyon (1895).
Format: DCP.
Finnish Frustrations (Eija Kaarresalo-Kasari, 1969, 7 min)
Diminishing dances. The last chance for women and men to find a partner. In seven minutes, this feminist cornerstone of Finnish cinema isolates an aspect of sexual inequality with a narrative starkness.
Format: DCP.
The Liar (Mika Kaurismäki, 1981, 53 min)
Mika Kaurismäki’s debut film set the tone for his groundbreaking Finnish cinema of the following decades. Ville Alfa (Aki Kaurismäki) is a lazy, young student vainly trying to finish his first proletarian novel. He likes to walk the streets of Helsinki, tell stories, spin lies and scam money off his friends. All for more drink and more women. Then one day, he meets Tuula (Pirkko Hämäläinen) and tries to change. A witty tribute to Jean-Luc Godard, and a delightful discovery for many.
Format: 35mm.
Total duration: approx. 2.5 hours including interval.
MUSICIANS
Lau Nau
Lau Nau, AKA Laura Naukkarinen, is a Finnish composer and sound artist whose music is imbued with an idiosyncratic, finely honed, sonic world view. Her palette often consists of traditional instruments, singing voice, modular synthesisers and field recordings.
Releasing albums on record labels in Europe, US and Japan, Lau Nau has toured internationally for 25 years. Venues such as the Castro Theatre in San Francisco, Super Deluxe in Tokyo, and NYC’s Knitting Factory have all welcomed her music. Lau Nau has played live accompaniment to silent films at festivals such as Midnight Sun Film Festival, San Francisco Silent Film Festival and Bologna’s Il Cinema Ritrovato.
Henri Utan K
Henri Utan K [ˈhɛn⟨r⟩ɪ uːtʌn kɒ] is the moniker of Finnish-born, London-based experimental guitarist and composer Henri Växby. On the fringes of the new music scene since the early 00s, his work moves between part-improvisation and full composition, combining stark dissonance with gently hypnotic soundscapes and ambient drones.
Henri studied composition at Goldsmiths University under Prof. Roger Redgate and at City St George’s University under Dr Claudia Molitor. He has been featured on BBC 6 Music, BBC Radio 3, at the Rainy Days Festival and Cafe OTO. Henri is also co-leader of avant-pop duo French For Cartridge and Finnish, post-Beatles outfit Icons of Elegance.
The event is supported by the Finnish Institute in the UK and Ireland.

rows.title: Bodies Adrift: Miami
rows.description:
Both from 1981, Tent City and Mayami Nuestro present contrasting and penetrating non-fiction portraits of Latin American diaspora communities in Miami.
Over several months in 1980, some 120,000 Cubans left their island for the United States in a mass exodus known as the Mariel boatlift. Fifteen years after having left Cuba herself, Miñuca Villaverde, alongside her husband Fernando visited the so-called “Tent City”, an improvised camp of these marielitos beneath the I-95 highway in Miami. Tent City explores that microcosm and reveals the day-to-day life of several refugees, “men and women, homosexuals and heterosexuals, whose lives were only separated by cloth curtains hanging between the beds like floating walls”. Empathetic but refusing victimhood, moving and reflexive, Tent City is one of the essential films about the Cuban diaspora, a portrait of people discarded by history in their incessant search for agency and liberty.
Carlos Oteyza’s Mayami Nuestro, meanwhile, takes a satirical yet affectionate look at Venezuela’s elite, capturing the exodus of petro-dollars from Venezuela to Miami in the 1980s. Contrasting Venezuela’s social inequalities with Miami’s sanitised consumerism, the film humorously registers both a frivolous neocolonial fantasy as well as a fleeting reversal of global capitalist hierarchies, when oil wealth gave the Venezuelan upper classes unprecedented power. With millions of Venezuelans in recent years traversing the Darién Gap in search of opportunity in the US, Mayami Nuestro resonates anew, highlighting the persistence of economic and cultural hierarchies in the Americas and beyond.
Programme
Tent City, dir. Miñuca Villaverde, USA 1981, 31 min.
Mayami Nuestro, dir. Carlos Oteyza, USA 1981, 33 min.
Total runtime: 64 min.
Presented by Jonathan Ali, José Luis Aparicio and Cinema Mentiré. With thanks to Cinesa, Francisco Llinas, Filmoteca de Catalunya and Fernando and Miñuca Villaverde.
Cinema Mentiré is a pop-up film club bringing a taste of rare classic and contemporary Latin American films to UK audiences.
Jonathan Ali is a film curator and writer with a particular interest in critical Caribbean cinema.

rows.title: La Raison Avant La Passion + A&B in Ontario on 16mm
rows.description:
La Raison Avant La Passion dir. Joyce Wieland, Canada 1969, 16mm, 80 min
A Canadian road trip and Pierre Trudeau's titular political motto provide the framework for Joyce Wieland's groundbreaking exploration of landscape, language and national identity. A journey from east coast to west coast, punctuated by an ambiguous portrait of the country's next prime minister, captures changing days and seasons at the same time as subverting the traditional travelogue and expanding the possibilities of structuralist film.
"Joyce Wieland’s rarely screened 1969 masterpiece is a neglected landmark of avant-garde film." – Fred Camper
A&B in Ontario dir. Joyce Wieland and Hollis Frampton, Canada 1984, 16mm, 16min
In 1967, Joyce Wieland and Hollis Frampton documented a holiday in Toronto by using Bolex wind-up cameras to play a game of hide-and-seek. Seventeen years later, Wieland, having been sent Frampton's reel after his death, assembled and edited the footage. The result is a lighthearted portrait of both filmmakers, whose often-mirrored point-of-view shots move from domestic spaces into the city and then the waterfront.
"We followed each other around. We enjoyed ourselves. We said we were going to make a film about each other, and we did." – Joyce Wieland
Total runtime: 96 min.

rows.title: HKFFUK 2026: Whose Family - Filipino Domestic Workers in Hong Kong and Beyond + Discussion
rows.description:
There are nearly 400,000 domestic migrant workers in Hong Kong, most of them women from the Philippines and Indonesia. The lack of a legal cap on working hours, alongside the live-in requirement, subjects these workers to overwork and cramped living conditions, and leaves them more vulnerable to physical and emotional abuse.
This Pay-What-You-Can community screening reflects on the labour conditions of Filipino domestic migrant workers in Hong Kong and the UK. Followed by a discussion over Hong Kong and Filipino snacks with Rose Ann Cotitob at The Voice of Domestic Workers.
The Model Family Award Germany, Philippines | 2008 | Colour | 12’ | In English and Filipino with English subtitles Dir.: Lizza May David
Every year in the Philippines, awards are given to ‘the most outstanding Filipino workers and their families for their exceptional achievements’. Artist Lizza May David captures the irony behind this glamorisation of a national labour-export policy built on the disruption of family life.
We Don’t Dance For Nothing Hong Kong, Canada, Philippines, USA
| 2022 | 87’ | Colour | In Cantonese, English, Filipino with English subtitles Dir.: Stefanos Tai
“There were so many fighting to be free, but I wondered — how many of them went home to dinner cooked by someone like me?” We Don't Dance For Nothing follows H
(Miles Sible), a Filipina domestic worker caring for a family of four in the city, at a time when hundreds of thousands of people are marching in the streets, demanding their freedom. H dreams of freedom too: a life where she can run away with her girlfriend Sampa (Xyza Cada). Her own life feels constantly on pause for the lives of others, a rhythm filmmaker Stefanos Tai renders through photo-montage — one that only finds its flow again when she is dancing.
Rose Ann Cotitob is a proud migrant domestic worker and campaigner with The Voice of Domestic Workers. She is originally from the Philippines and today works as a nanny and housekeeper in Hackney. In 2023, her employer brought her to London and she was later identified as a victim of modern slavery.

Hong Kong Film Festival UK returns for its fourth edition from 25 September to 4 October in London, presenting reflective and shape-shifting cinema from Hong Kong, the wider Asian diaspora and beyond, marking the start of a more year-round festival.
This year’s programme foregrounds diaspora as agency — behind the camera, on screen and between communities. Across contemporary and historical cinema, artists’ moving image and interdisciplinary art practices, the festival moves through questions of migration, colonisation, activism and gender. rows.title: Site&Sound 12 – Suburbs
rows.description:
Site&Sound is an event series that explores the relationship between architecture and film. Each session will feature curated clips and short films around a chosen theme, inviting discussion around particular elements of representation and the different techniques employed by filmmakers. Themes will examine a multitude of perspectives on architecture, as we explore a world through the lens of the built environment.

“What the hell, I don’t know, but to me a home in the suburbs is a sort of isolated hell where nothing happens” – Jack Kerouac

The suburbs appear as a place of safety and order, often depicted with row upon row of identikit houses and manicured lawns. However, films understand that there is more beneath the surface, which is often weird, wonderful and a bit disturbing.  You can argue that suburbs are built on exclusion, when anything outside the narrow bounds of acceptable becomes threatening and intolerable. Prejudices based on race, sexuality, class and even appearance lead to ideas that such nonconformity must be contained, denied or expelled.

The juxtaposition of banal and weird emerges from this tension, with the suburbs’ visual perfection becoming a container for secrets. But perhaps it is the normality that is the true mask. To combat this, cinema creates outliers – such as Edward Scissorhands – to figure out what happens when their appearance challenges the landscape of artificial perfection, and the response is often swift and brutal. The Incredibles reverses it, as a superhero family performs mundane suburban life while harbouring extraordinary secrets, using the domestic space to cover for their radical difference.

This edition of Site&Sound will examine how the suburb’s visual serenity sets the scene for what happens when people cannot (or will not) fit the mould.

Rosie Dart
John Grindrod
Sofia Smith

The definitive insight into the real lives of Britain’s most notorious gangsters, from their trusted official biographer. For decades they were feared as the ultimate criminal gang lords of the London underworld, but their reign of terror came crashing to an end when in 1969 both Ronnie and Reggie Kray were given life sentences by a judge at the Old Bailey. This year, the London Breeze Film Festival Industry Programme shines a spotlight on the art of music and sound with a special afternoon dedicated to exploring their creative impact on filmmaking.

A love letter to pre-gentrification Brooklyn, the film celebrates a time when music was driven by experimentation, survival and an unbreakable sense of community.

rows.description:
We're thrilled to welcome Booker prize-winning author Marlon James to The Ritzy to celebrate the release of his new novel, The Disappearers: a triumphant return to the Jamaica of A Brief History of Seven Killings – a place of heat and chaos, and of danger for anyone outside the heteronormal.
 
James will appear live in conversation on the night and will be signing copies of The Disappearers after the screening.
 
Presented as part of Picturehouse's Book Club: bringing your bookshelf to the big screens. Join us for curated screenings and events, conversations with literary minds, and more.
 
Marlon James is the author of the New York Times bestselling Moon Witch, Spider King; the Sunday Times bestselling, National Book Award-finalist Black Leopard, Red Wolf; the Booker Prize-winning A Brief History of Seven Killings; The Book of Night Women and John Crow's Devil. In addition to the Booker Prize, his novels have won the American Book Award, the Los Angeles Times Ray Bradbury Prize for Science Fiction, the Anisfield-Wolf Award and the Dayton Literary Peace Prize. Born in Jamaica, Marlon James now lives in New York City.
 
 
ABOUT THE DISAPPEARERS
 
When eight gay men meet for the first time, in Kingston in 1988, answering the casting call for an openly queer play, they are already taking a big risk. But that is nothing compared to what rains down on them when a mob descends on one of their rehearsals. By the end of this night, one man is dead, all are injured, and two subsequently disappear.
 
As the survivors heal, each man finds he must confront the bigotry and homophobia that the attack laid bare. Some try to forget; some embrace their rage; and some simply vanish – but all are forever scarred. As one of the victims puts it, ‘there’s a difference between when something ends and when something stops’. And this story won’t stop until both the disappearers and the perpetrators have been tracked, along trails both hot and cold, and an ending reached.
 
Epic and intimate, violent and forgiving, The Disappearers is a tour de force which only Marlon James could have written – both an unflinching portrait of the hatred and shame faced by gay men in a society which refuses to accept them, and a deeply human story of acceptance and insight.
 
 
Presented in partnership with Dark Matter.

rows.title: Lumière! The Adventure Continues
rows.description:
130 years ago, the Lumière brothers invented cinema. Everything was already there: the composition, tracking shots, dramatic scenes, comedy sketches, actors… Thanks to the restoration of over 100 previously unseen Lumière ‘views’ –comedies, dramas, and travelogues –Thierry Frémaux offers us a spectacle of the world at the turn of the century and a stimulating journey to the origins of the moving image, of cinema through the pioneering achievements of the French entrepreneurs Auguste and Louis Lumière 
Thierry Frémaux, the director of the Cannes Film Festival, the Institut Lumière, and the Lumière Film Festival in Lyon, France, the birthplace of these remarkable brothers, brings a wealth of insight, history, and revelation to this journey back to the 1890s, when the Lumière Company, with their astonishing new invention, the cinematograph, made it possible for audiences to voyage around the world in moving pictures for the first time. Set to an evocative score of period music by Gabriel Fauré, this wondrous documentary enables contemporary viewers to imagine an entirely new language of storytelling unfolding film by glorious film.

Audrey Niffeneger is a visual artist and writer who has published six books, including the novels The Time Traveler’s Wife and Her Fearful Symmetry. She is also a Professor in the Fiction Department of Columbia College.
ABOUT LIFE OUT OF ORDER 
Two great loves. A world in chaos. And a life that never lands in order. Alba DeTamble is a time traveler, slipping unpredictably through decades like her father before her.
But the hardest thing she carries isn’t the burden of futures she can’t understand, or pasts she cannot change – it’s a secret: she is in love with two different people. Each of them offers a different life. Zach lives in the present and can’t follow her when she disappears. Oliver can travel through time, just like she can. 
As Alba careens from time to time, she must face a question she can no longer avoid: how is it possible to love, and live a meaningful life, in an increasingly troubled, fractured world? Intimate and expansive, Life Out of Order is a kaleidoscopic story of love, resilience and hope when time is running out.

rows.title: UK Premiere: The Magic of It All - The Story of Strawbs + Q&A with director & Derek "Blue" Weaver
rows.description:
A legacy built on music. A journey defined by resilience. A final act no one saw coming.

In 2022, Dave Cousins, frontman of British folk-rock pioneers Strawbs, travelled to Cape Town for what was intended to be a simple recording session. Instead, facing cancer, he delayed treatment and endured eight months of isolation to complete his swansong. Featuring Rick Wakeman and Tony Visconti, this intimate documentary captures an extraordinary period of artistic rebirth, friendship and sacrifice, culminating in a triumphant final performance before 25,000 fans in Oxford. The Magic of It All is a moving tribute to Strawbs and the transcendent power of music in the face of mortality.

rows.description:
Can classical music be humorous? Absolutely! 
The Berliner Philharmoniker and their chief conductor Kirill Petrenko will demonstrate this at the 2026 New Year’s Eve Concert: in his sparkling Symphonie classique, Sergei Prokofiev parodies the music of Haydn and Mozart.
Dmitri Shostakovich also had the First Viennese School in mind when he wrote his witty Double Concerto for Piano and Trumpet. 
In this performance, pianist Alexander Malofeev, born in 2001, makes his debut alongside principal trumpeter David Guerrier.

rows.title: The Attic Comedy Club
rows.description:
Big screens. Bigger laughs. Join us at The Attic at Hackney Picturehouse for a monthly night of fresh comedy from some of the most exciting names in the game! There’ll be quality jokes, plus delicious food and drink waiting at our bar. (If all else fails, you can at least go and see a film instead.)
We're delighted to welcome Finlay Christie, Cecily Hitchcock, Helen Bauer, and MC Raul Kohli to our next night of stand up comedy on Saturday the 19th of September.
Finlay ChristieFinlay misguidedly believes that his muggers fancied him, that being a f*ckboy is cool and that Kim Jong Un would love him. Funny, self-aware and internet-brained, this is an hour about the myths constructed by incels, billionaires and even human people, that mean we don’t have to admit we’re ordinary, rejected or wrong. There’s also a strong section on air fryers. As seen on social media (1M+ followers), Live at the Apollo, Have I Got News For You and 8 Out of 10 Cats Does Countdown. 'The voice of a generation' **** (Chortle.co.uk).
Cecily Hitchcock

Cecily Hitchcock is a comedy siren, crowd enchantress & heckler annihilator. Her unique mix of outlandish anecdotes and off-beat observations have gained traction both online and on stage. Cecily is an accomplished live M.C and her sketches and stand up videos have amassed over 25 million views on social media and have been featured on Ladbible, The Sidemen & Brewdog. She is making her highly anticipated Edinburgh Fringe debut in 2026 with her show ‘Family Recipe’.
“Outstanding” – The Independent
“Hot” – Katherine Ryan
 

Helen Bauer
Helen Bauer, started making comedy sketches in London and Berlin, when she lived there, and came to prominence as a finalist in the 2018 BBC New Comedy Award.Her debut show, Little Miss Baby Angel Face, was nominated for best newcomer in the 2019 Dave's Edinburgh Comedy Award. She made her debut on Live At The Apollo in 2021.
 
Raul Kohli Raul Kohli is one of the most captivating acts in UK comedy. Growing up Indian in Newcastle upon Tyne, he’s developed a worldview that playfully upends ethnicity, culture and class, combining what The Scotsman called “superb political comedy” with surreal storytelling. His debut show was selected as a top pick of Edinburgh Fringe 2016 by BBC Radio 4, The Huffington Post and The Skinny. He was nominated for Best Show at Leicester Comedy Festival 2019, and his 2024 Edinburgh Fringe show (Ish Awards) was hailed by Chortle as “one of the most important shows of the fringe,” with jokes featured in The Guardian and The Daily Mail’s Top Ten of the Fringe.

rows.title: Rhapsody on the Outlaw Ocean (London Breeze Film Festival UK Premiere + Q&A)
rows.description:
Rhapsody on the Outlaw Ocean (USA 61 min) Dir. Ian Urbina

And now for something completely different! As part of our IMPACT day, London Breeze is thrilled to present the UK premiere of writer director, Ian Urbina, and composer William Segal’s animated musical rap documentary exposing the lawless world of international waters, drawn from ten years of reporting and featuring vocal talent from Broadway’s Hamilton, including Sydney James Harcourt and Brandon Victor Dixon.

The film offers a rare window into an unseen world as well as one journalist’s attempt to find new ways to chronicle a place that feels too foreign, too hard to believe, to be captured through traditional means.

For over ten years, Pulitzer Prize-winning journalist, Ian Urbina, embarked on a journey to uncover the hidden truths of what happens on the high seas. Over 50 million people work offshore in a realm without governments, police or oversight. What he found was a hidden world. On the outlaw ocean, bad actors take advantage for their own gain, and good actors exploit legal loopholes to achieve what could never be done on land. The reporting behind these stories is stunning and important. Stowaways left out to die at sea. Vigilantes chasing an illegal fishing ship. A man recalling the trauma of being enslaved on a ship. Crimes against human rights, crimes against the environment — made possible through the void of government on the water that covers two thirds of the planet.

In Rhapsody on the Outlaw Ocean, these true and harrowing stories are rendered into an animated musical rap documentary, as we follow the path of the Journalist as he traverses the high seas by ship from Antarctica to the South China Sea to the North Atlantic and beyond, uncovering the unbelievable stories of the people who work on the world’s oceans.

+ Iridescence (FRA 4 min) Dir. Adrien Lhoste

A single drop of water is carried inside a bottle by a drone. It travels across a scorching, futuristic desert world where each place becomes increasingly dangerous. Along the way, it narrowly escapes a man with a net, a boxing kangaroo, and giant jellyfish… until it finally finds itself in the middle of a billionaire’s party.

rows.title: Being Human Dementia Film Club
rows.description:
Dementia Film Club How can collaborative filmmaking support active brain health? Join Vesna Lukic to explore the benefits of filmmaking for people living with dementia. Dementia Film Club at the Phoenix Cinema is an interactive and creative cinema workshop, where you will find out about the processes of making a film. There will be a screening of a work-in-progress film made with the Barnet Age UK Day Opportunities Centre, and you will be invited to give feedback and make suggestions for the next stages of the project. There will also be opportunities to learn how to handle cameras and record sound and images. Come along and be part of this creative process! This workshop is designed specifically to accommodate people living with dementia and their carers, and is open to anyone with an interest in filmmaking. Suitable for all ages.
This event is part of Being Human Festival, the UK’s national festival of the humanities, taking place 5-14 November 2026. Led by the School of Advanced Study, University of London, in partnership with the Arts and Humanities Research Council and the British Academy. For further information please see beinghumanfestival.org

rows.title: Kendal Mountain Festival: The Film Edit
rows.description:
Join us for a special evening celebrating the spirit of adventure, with a lovingly curated selection of films fresh from the Kendal Mountain Festival. Bringing together powerful stories from around the world, this collection features stunning landscapes, people, passion, and a shared love of the outdoors that connects us all. Whether it’s climbing, running, exploring, or simply finding joy in wild places, these films reflect the experiences that resonate close to home. Can’t make it to Kendal? Come along, meet fellow enthusiasts, and be inspired together. It’s a chance to gather, connect, and celebrate the adventurous spirit that makes our community special.
About Kendal Mountain Festival: Established in 1980, Kendal Mountain Festival celebrates all aspects of outdoor and adventure culture. An internationally-acclaimed gathering for filmmakers, writers, adventurers, and enthusiasts, the Festival showcases films, talks, exhibitions, and activities that inspire a love for the outdoors. Kendal Mountain is a global platform for sharing stories of nature, exploration, adventure, and discovery. During the four-day Festival, held 19-22nd November 2026, over 200 live sessions – including 300+ speakers, 150+ films, and 60+ activities – engage over 25,000 adventure-seekers and outdoor enthusiasts.
Films:
Surfing with a Penguin 8 mins | Director: Will Bendix From sharks and seals to whales and everything in between, Cape Town, South Africa, is renowned for wildlife encounters in the water. But it is rare for surfers to see a penguin, let alone share a few waves with one - until this little guy came along. Virtus: The Four P's 11 mins | Director: Toby Roney Virtus centres on Ed Jackson's climb of the Matterhorn, but at its heart, it is not really about the mountain. It is about the values that have shaped Ed's life after trauma: purpose, perspective, progress and perseverance. Through scenes from the climb, moments from recovery and connections with the Millimetres to Mountains community, the film explores how challenge can rebuild identity, deepen perspective and create meaningful growth. It Takes Two to Tandem 6 mins | Directors: Catherine Aeppel and Anna Wilder-Burns This feel-good short follows longtime riding partners Sam and Jazz as they take a tandem bike across some of their favourite trails, marking ten years since their first tandem adventure together. Part celebration and part reflection, the film explores friendship, trust and the rare joy of moving through the world in sync. Zuma Rock 34 mins | Director: Luke Logan-Malik Rotimi, an amateur climber and writer from London with deep family roots in Nigeria, sets out to achieve the unthinkable: the first ascent of Zuma Rock, a 300-metre monolith considered sacred by the communities living in its shadow. To do it, he enlists Olympic climbing champion Shauna Coxsey - but neither of them has ever tackled a wall of this scale. Find Mor 28 mins | Director: Steve Small Exploration. Community. Discovery. Scotland's mysteries are still roaring through remote glens, sometimes hidden in plain sight. Find Mor follows a group of canyoneers over two years as they explore the hidden corners of the Scottish Highlands. Offering a unique perspective from within this relatively unknown community, the film reveals the many motivations behind their shared passion and curiosity. They set off in search of uncharted canyons, but find true adventure and a deeper connection to people and place. "You come for the canyons but stay for the people." Hunter's Moon 14 mins | Directors: Christina Lusti and Gee Pierrel Mountaineers Christina Lusti and Gee Pierrel attempt to become the first people to summit and ski New Zealand's Aoraki / Mount Cook via a line they name Hunter's Moon .
